_about: Chapter 1's boss: the beholder of level 1-32 (level31), as the original's own script
plays it. Every number here not marked _guess is decoded from android_game.bin, the
(bytes 374987..380209), its globals, and the helpers it calls. The owner's account of
the fight (11 September) agrees with it, except for the spikes: they remember five, in
random directions, every 1.5 s. The script fires ten, 40 degrees apart and turned by
10 every other time, every 1.2 s. The script is followed. See

_source: An adder marker spawns the entity its custom data names, where it stands
(ETHCallback_adder, Adder.angelscript, bytes 372581..372886); level31's names
beholder.ent. BEHOLDER_MAX_HP is 2 and BEHOLDER_RADIUS 48 (SetG4 in their
initialisers, bytes 298296 and 298355). It starts with hp 2 and dies when hp is -1
or less, so it takes three hits. A rolling stone within the radius and rising (its
velocity against (0, -1) above 0) breaks and hurts it; the player within it dies.
BEHOLDER_STATE_SEEKING. It aims at its own x plus the player's offset in x clamped
to 64 px, and at its start height plus 8 px times cos(elapsedTime + PIb), and goes
there by followUp: a PositionInterpolator over 2000 ms filtered by smoothEnd,
sin(v * PIb), taken up again from where it is once more than 1000 ms have passed.
When the player has been within 32 px of its x for more than 400 ms it shuts its
eye and throws rocks.
BEHOLDER_STATE_THROW_ROCK, for more than 7900 ms. overTimeEntityAdder drops
rolling_stone.ent at the player's x and y -32 every 2000 ms, on a clock this state
never resets. So a later round's first rock can come early, and the round hold
four: that is the original's, and kept. Meanwhile linearMotion bobs it by 4 px
times cos(angle), the angle from PIb at 2 radians a second.
BEHOLDER_STATE_GOT_DAMAGE, for more than 7200 ms. Every 1200 ms it fires
beholder_spike.ent from its centre at every 40 degrees from 0 to 360 inclusive,
clockwise from up, turned by 10 degrees every other time: ten spikes, two of them the
same way. addProjectileEntity gives each 140 px/s.
BEHOLDER_STATE_DEAD. Once dead for more than 3550 ms it explodes (explode, with a
radius of 80 px, which kills the player in it), the level's button is put at its
button_dest, and the beholder goes.
ETHCallback_beholder_spike (bytes 374024..374987). A spike flies on through
everything, is deleted once outside the screen grown by 16 x 128 px, and kills a
character whose size times 0.7, centred on it, holds the spike's point. dark_mage.ent's
frame is 40 x 56 (magic_portals_hd.png, 160 x 224, cut 4 x 4).
_cull_note: The original culls against the screen. The port's level has no camera, so it culls
against the level's extent, (0, 0) to its level_bounds marker, grown by the same

_source: ETHBeginContactCallback_rolling_stone (MiscCallbacks.angelscript, bytes
346486..347456). A stone's intensity is its velocity along the line to what it
touches, divided by the global scale. Above 2.5 it kills a character, and a stone with
destroyOnStaticHit set - every one overTimeEntityAdder drops - breaks on anything
static it runs into (intensity above 0). The velocity is Box2D's, at 50 px to the unit
(ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:27), divided once by the global scale
(ETHPhysicsController.cpp:122).
_guess_note: The unit, and the margin; not the threshold. The script divides by the global scale a
second time, so on a device the threshold moved with the screen. The port takes the
scale as 1, the original's 480 px reference height (DEFAULT_SCALE_HEIGHT). The margin
is how near a rock has to come to count as touching. BeginContact fires when Box2D's
shapes touch; the engine's solver stops a fast body short of what it is closing on
(speculative contacts, PhysicsSystem.cpp), and a rock falling onto the player at 571
px/s was measured left 1.0 px above its head. So 2 px, a port threshold.
